transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just done your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So if it's been at least a week since your operation, you're good to go ahead with that.

Just avoid anything too strenuous or heavy for about a month after surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you don't have any left or you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That'll help me give you a better idea of what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about two weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Thank you for letting me know. At two weeks, your vision should be improving well by now. Some mild blurriness can still be present, but it should be getting clearer.

However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and all the best with your recovery.

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting with "It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light...". However, the `escalation_criteria` point was not conveyed at any point in the conversation.
